name: Cerebrolysin

card.summary: A porcine brain-derived peptide mixture approved for stroke and dementia in many countries, discussed by forum users as an "iqmaxxing" nootropic.
card.note: Injectable prescription product; nootropic use in healthy people is not studied.

quick.overview:
Cerebrolysin is an injectable mixture of low-molecular-weight peptides and amino acids prepared from porcine brain protein. It is marketed by EVER Neuro Pharma in Austria and used in many countries as an adjunct for stroke, brain injury and dementia.

On looksmax.org it appears in threads about "iqmaxxing" and "brainmaxxing", where members ask whether it helps studying or exams. It is not an appearance compound, and no studies have tested it in healthy people for cognition.
quick.mechanism: Preclinical studies report that it mimics neurotrophic factor activity and promotes neurogenesis in rodent stroke and Alzheimer models, including through the Sonic hedgehog pathway.
quick.risks: Human trials are in patients with neurological disease. Being an animal-derived injectable, it is a prescription product where approved; members mention obtaining it from unofficial sources.

lead: Cerebrolysin is an injectable mixture of low-molecular-weight peptides and free amino acids made by enzymatic breakdown of porcine brain protein, produced by EVER Neuro Pharma in Austria and described as mimicking the activity of neurotrophic factors.[1][4] Wikipedia lists its development code as FPF-1070 and says it may contain fragments resembling BDNF, GDNF, NGF and CNTF.[16] It is given by infusion or injection and is used in many countries as an adjunct in stroke, traumatic brain injury and dementia.[1][22][21]

Cerebrolysin is not an appearance compound. Its place in looksmaxxing culture is under the 'iqmaxxing' or 'brainmaxxing' banner: members who treat intelligence, exam performance and learning as part of 'ascending' ask whether it can sharpen studying, language learning and test results.[12][13][14][15] The chain they describe is: a neurotrophic peptide mixture, then better neuroplasticity and memory, then better study and exam output. The one appearance-adjacent item in the literature is a five-person registered study of hair repigmentation during Cerebrolysin therapy.[11]

The research is in patients. Randomised trials, Cochrane reviews and meta-analyses cover stroke, vascular dementia and brain injury, with mixed conclusions: a nine-trial meta-analysis reported better stroke recovery scores at 30 days, while the 2023 Cochrane update found no meaningful difference in death and a higher rate of non-fatal serious adverse events.[6][17][25] No published trial has tested it in healthy people for cognition or for appearance outcomes.

chain: Injected peptide mixture from porcine brain
Proponents expect better learning and memory
angle.text: Forum members consider Cerebrolysin for studying and exams, treating cognitive performance as part of overall self-improvement. The mechanism they cite is its neurotrophic reputation; human trials were done in neurological patients, not in healthy students.

paras: Cerebrolysin is an aqueous solution of peptides with molecular weights below roughly 10,000 daltons together with free amino acids, produced by treating porcine brain tissue with proteases, filtering and sterilising it.[1] Grokipedia and a pharmacology review describe it as a neuropeptide preparation that mimics endogenous neurotrophic factors, with trace amounts of factors such as BDNF, GDNF, NGF and CNTF reported in the mixture.[1][4][16] Because it is an animal-derived biological mixture, its exact active constituents are not fully defined; Wikipedia says its specific molecular actions are unclear.[16]

Grokipedia dates the origin to 1949, when Gerhart Harrer at the University of Innsbruck pioneered enzymatic hydrolysis of brain tissue, with clinical use in the 1950s and systematic trials and post-marketing surveillance from the 1970s; it is now manufactured by EVER Neuro Pharma (formerly Ebewe Pharma).[1][19] These dates are reported by Grokipedia alone.[16]

The preparation became established in Russia, Eastern Europe, China and other Asian and post-Soviet countries, where Cochrane describes it as widely used in acute ischaemic stroke.[17][19] In English-language forums the name spread through 'nootropics' and research-peptide communities, usually alongside Semax and Selank.[13]

Laboratory studies in rats reported that Cerebrolysin increased neurogenesis after experimental stroke and improved functional outcome, and that the Sonic hedgehog pathway mediated this effect.[2][5] A pharmacology review states that in dementia models it reduced beta-amyloid deposition and tau phosphorylation by regulating GSK-3 beta and CDK5 activity.[4] Wikipedia says laboratory studies suggest neurotrophic effects resembling endogenous mechanisms and notes that some neurotrophic components are very short-lived in blood, which it illustrates with a BDNF half-life of about 10 minutes.[16]

Cerebrolysin is used in many countries for acute ischaemic stroke, traumatic brain injury and dementia, usually as a course of infusions.[1][22][21] Wikipedia lists early-stage research in schizophrenia, multiple sclerosis, cerebral palsy and spinal cord injury and says it is not recommended for people with epilepsy, kidney disease or hypersensitivity to its components.[16] It is described as prescription-only, with an unclear approval status in several countries and no US approval.[16]

The CARS trial gave stroke patients 30 mL per day of Cerebrolysin or saline for 21 days starting 24-72 hours after onset, alongside standardised rehabilitation. Its primary endpoint, upper-limb motor function (Action Research Arm Test) at day 90, favoured Cerebrolysin with a Mann-Whitney estimate of 0.71; the authors described the study as exploratory and called for a larger confirmatory trial.[3][25]

A meta-analysis of nine double-blind trials (1,879 patients on the NIH Stroke Scale at day 30, with treatment begun within 72 hours) reported a Mann-Whitney effect of 0.60 favouring Cerebrolysin and comparable safety to placebo.[6][25] The 2023 Cochrane update included seven Cerebrolysin trials (1,773 participants) and reported no meaningful difference in all-cause death (risk ratio 0.96), no clear difference in total serious adverse events, but more non-fatal serious adverse events (risk ratio 2.39); it concluded Cerebrolysin probably does not prevent death.[17][25] A double-blind trial in Asian patients with acute ischaemic stroke and an open-label add-on study with mechanical thrombectomy have also been reported.[7][23] Registered studies include a stroke registry and trials of the drug around thrombolysis or thrombectomy.[8][28]

The 2019 Cochrane review of vascular dementia included six trials (597 participants). Pooled cognitive data from three studies favoured Cerebrolysin (standardised mean difference 0.36) and two studies showed a higher global-function response; the authors rated the findings as very low quality, noted high risk of bias and said any benefit may be too small to be clinically meaningful.[18][25] A 2025 meta-analysis of 173 trials in vascular cognitive impairment reported small to moderate cognitive improvements for several interventions, Cerebrolysin among them, with substantial methodological heterogeneity.[20][25]

A 2025 review lists Cerebrolysin among neuroprotective options being evaluated after moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury.[21] A randomised trial in high-risk preterm infants examined neurodevelopmental outcomes with Cerebrolysin plus a routine intervention programme, and registered studies include Down syndrome, preterm infants, postoperative delirium in cardiac surgery and hair repigmentation.[24][9][10][27][11] No studies found in healthy people for cognitive enhancement or appearance outcomes.

Wikipedia reports nausea, dizziness, headache and sweating among reported effects and says it is not recommended in epilepsy or kidney disease; it also notes inconsistency in how the stroke safety data are described.[16] The 2023 Cochrane update found no clear difference in total adverse events but an increase in non-fatal serious adverse events, particularly in one dosing subgroup.[17] Earlier trials and the nine-trial meta-analysis reported safety comparable to placebo.[3][6] Because it is an injectable made from animal tissue, product quality and sterility depend on the source, a point forum members themselves raise when discussing unofficial supply.[12]

On looksmax.org, Cerebrolysin appears in a handful of threads: a member weighing it before a university admissions exam, a thread headed as a deep dive into 'iqmaxxing', a 2021 question about using it to 'brainmaxx', and a thread on whether Semax, Selank and Cerebrolysin are 'cope'.[12][13][14][15] In the 'cope' thread, one reply says nootropics do improve learning and studying capability, while another jokingly recommends amphetamines.[13] Members typically ask about timing, dose and sourcing, which this article does not cover.[12]

A 2026 survey of Romanian university students, listed in the literature, examines predictors of psychoactive and nootropic substance use among students, illustrating the wider study-enhancement context in which such products are discussed.[26]

Cerebrolysin is a prescription medicine where approved and is used mainly in Europe, Russia and Asia; Wikipedia states it is not an approved drug in the United States.[16][1] Research-peptide vendors sell lyophilised versions outside medical channels, according to Grokipedia.[1]

Registered trials include add-on treatment after endovascular stroke therapy, effects on the blood-brain barrier in acute ischaemic stroke, postoperative delirium and basilar artery occlusion.[28][27] A 2026 review of regulatory positions on nootropics in Alzheimer's disease and other recent papers reflect continuing interest.[26]

timeline.event: Grokipedia credits Gerhart Harrer at Innsbruck with pioneering enzymatic hydrolysis of brain tissue.[1]
Grokipedia dates first clinical studies of the preparation to around this year.[1]
Rat study reports increased neurogenesis after embolic stroke with Cerebrolysin.[2]
Rat study reports the Sonic hedgehog pathway mediates the effect.[5]
CARS randomised trial of Cerebrolysin after stroke is published; Cochrane stroke review also updated.[3][19]
Meta-analysis of nine randomised stroke trials published.[6]
Cochrane review of Cerebrolysin in vascular dementia.[18]
A looksmax.org member asks about using it to 'brainmaxx'.[15]
Cochrane stroke update reports no difference in death and more non-fatal serious adverse events; 'iqmaxxing' deep-dive thread appears.[17][14]
Meta-analysis of vascular cognitive impairment trials and a review of neuroprotection after brain injury include Cerebrolysin.[20][21]

lore.intro: Cerebrolysin appears in looksmax.org nootropic threads, typically in questions about studying and exams, and alongside Semax and Selank.[12][13][14]

claims.claim: Cerebrolysin boosts intelligence and study performance ('iqmaxxing').
claims.believers: Members consider it for exams and language learning, and one reply in a nootropics thread says nootropics increase learning and studying capability.[12][13][14]
claims.experts: Published human trials are in neurological patients; no published studies have tested it for cognitive enhancement in healthy people.[25]

claims.claim: It supports brain recovery and neurogenesis.
claims.experts: Rodent studies report increased neurogenesis; a nine-trial meta-analysis found better stroke scores, while the 2023 Cochrane update found no difference in death and more non-fatal serious adverse events.[2][5][6][17]

claims.claim: Nootropics like Cerebrolysin are 'cope' and not worth ascension effort.
claims.believers: A poster says people keep telling him nootropics are 'cope'; others reply that they work for learning.[13]
claims.experts: No studies compare nootropic use with other study aids in healthy students; a 2026 survey examines predictors of student nootropic use.[26]
